purpose: Who is on the public record on the 136th General Assembly bills that rewrote or would change Ohio’s voter-passed adult-use law: committee testimony, lobbying activity reports, IRS Form 990 filings of the trade and advocacy groups that testified, and the Ohio Cannabis Coalition’s own statements. Owner direction, November 24, 2026. Every entry is drawn from the official record named with it; secondary sources are not used.
rules: Every organization and every side is shown in the same format.

People appear only in the public role an official record gives them: committee witness, registered lobbying agent, or an officer, director or employee listed on a Form 990. No home addresses, personal contact details or private information.
Witnesses who testified for themselves (organization listed as “Self” or left blank) are not named here; the official document carries the name.
Quotes are verbatim from the witness’s or organization’s own document and are the first clear statement of position found there. Open the document for the full text.
A lobbying activity report shows that an employer lobbied on a bill in a period. It does not show a position.
Elected officials’ party, votes and sponsorships are on each lawmaker’s card.

bills.title: Revise medical and adult-use marijuana laws; levy marijuana taxes
bills.why: The 136th General Assembly bill that rewrote the adult-use law voters passed as Issue 2 in November 2023 (Revised Code Chapter 3780).
bills.status: Final agreement: House, November 19, 2025; Senate, December 9, 2025. OHCANN’s statement of March 19, 2026 says it took effect March 20, 2026.

bills.title: Revise liquor control, hemp, and adult-use marijuana laws
bills.why: The House’s own 136th General Assembly rewrite of the Issue 2 law, heard alongside SB 56. Included because it is the bill on which OHCANN filed testimony.
bills.status: Introduced March 6, 2025; referred to House Judiciary March 19, 2025; three hearings; no later action shown on the status page.

bills.title: Issue medical marijuana processor cultivation, dispensary license
bills.why: Would issue paired cultivator and dispensary licenses to certain medical marijuana processors (long title: “to issue paired cultivator and dispensary licenses to certain medical marijuana processors”).
bills.status: Introduced November 25, 2025; passed the House June 10, 2026 (87–5); referred to Senate General Government September 30, 2026. No Senate hearing is listed.

ohcann_membership.wayback_note: Snapshot links come from the Internet Archive availability service. The archive’s pages could not be opened from the retrieval environment on 2026-11-24 (connection reset), so earlier membership lists were not compared and no change in membership is inferred from them. No snapshot of the 2026-11-24 retrieval exists.
ohcann_membership.status_rule: Every company is shown as “Listed as OHCANN member (as of the retrieval date)”. A company is moved to “Left OHCANN” only with a dated source that says so.
ohcann_membership.directory_note: Directory record IDs refer to data/directory.json. The OhioWeed directory page does not open a single record by link, so the link opens the directory, where the name can be searched.

lobbyist_contributions.method: Federal contributions from the FEC individual-contributions API (Ohio addresses, January 2019 on), searched by surname and given name. A record is shown only when the employer named on it is an employer the agent is registered for at JLEC, or a firm the agent’s own firm or bio page confirms. Records that cannot be tied this way are left off. Addresses are used only to read the records and are never published. Ohio contributions are not included: the Secretary of State’s site and bulk files blocked retrieval.
lobbyist_contributions.order: Agents for OHCANN and OMCIA first, then agents for OHCANN member companies, then every other employer’s agents. The same rule applies to all.
lobbyist_contributions.bios_rule: Prior government or campaign roles and party ties appear only as the agent’s own firm, organization or bio page states them.
